title: Mixed geometric base-change and semilinear exchange pasting
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]. Let a Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes have vertical maps $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, $f'_0:X'_0\to Y'_0$ and horizontal maps $u_0:X'_0\to X_0$, $v_0:Y'_0\to Y_0$, all separated and of finite type. Use its geometric base change $(f,f',u,v)$, geometric-Galois automorphisms $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ on its four corners, where $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and $G_T=Lg_T^*$, $Q_X=Lu^*$, $Q_Y=Lv^*$. On the coefficient and constructible finite-Tor domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], write $F_f=Rf_!$, $F_{f'}=Rf'_!$ and let
$$B:Q_YF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}Q_X$$
be the specified compact-support base-change map. Let
$$e_f:G_YF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fG_X,\qquad e_{f'}:G_{Y'}F_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}G_{X'}$$
be the semilinear-isomorphism exchanges of [def-exchange-projection], evaluated over the respective base schemes $S=Y,Y'$. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ in these domains, under the canonical pullback identifications $Q_TG_T\cong G_{T'}Q_T$, the two maps from $Q_YG_YF_fM$ to $F_{f'}G_{X'}Q_XM$ agree:
$$B_{G_XM}\circ Q_Y(e_{f,M})=e_{f',Q_XM}\circ G_{Y'}(B_M).$$
Here the target of the left side is identified using $Q_XG_X\cong G_{X'}Q_X$. Each exchange is the actual compactification mate followed by the open-extension comparison. At integral coefficients the identity holds for the specified strict-tower transformations before derived limit, and at field coefficients it holds after scalar localization/common-stage passage. It is independent of the chosen compactification through the refinement comparisons on those same domains. This assertion includes arbitrary base changes within these domains; it imposes no $k$-linearity on the semilinear maps $g_T$.
